item.text: {"classifications":[{"segment_id":"1","code":1,"rationale":"The President introduces an internal assignment of executive functions to the Secretary of Defense; the heading itself does not alter substantive legal rights, and the assignment is specified in the following segment.","evidence":"Section 1. Assignment of Functions to the Secretary of Defense."},{"segment_id":"2","code":1,"rationale":"The President directs the Secretary of Defense to perform specified presidential functions, subject to stated exceptions; this is an immediate internal delegation of authority rather than a dictated substantive legal outcome.","evidence":"The Secretary of Defense shall perform"},{"segment_id":"3","code":1,"rationale":"The President assigns functions to the Secretary of Homeland Security and permits the two Secretaries to reassign certain functions within their departments; these are internal delegations and authority-allocation rules effective under the order.","evidence":"may reassign the functions assigned to them by this order to civilian officers"},{"segment_id":"4","code":1,"rationale":"The President sets the date when the order's internal delegations and organizational provisions become effective; the clause does not itself create a substantive legal consequence for regulated parties.","evidence":"This order shall take effect on October 1, 2004."}]}
